standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the property to be verified and the tool for the middle-term conclusion.

core_obligations: Recall the base-change characterization of quasi-coherence on the chaotic topology and set up the five-term exact sequence F_0 -> F_1 -> F_2 -> F_3 -> F_4 with the outer four terms quasi-coherent (proof lines 3606-3616).

For a morphism U -> V form the commutative diagram obtained by tensoring the sequence with O(U) over O(V), and use flatness of the restriction maps to keep the rows exact (proof lines 3617-3624 and following).

Apply the five lemma to conclude that the middle base-change map is an isomorphism, hence that F_2 is quasi-coherent, and conclude that the class is a weak Serre subcategory, completing the proof up to line 3641.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the base-change characterization of quasi-coherence.
Tensor the test sequence and keep exactness using flatness.
Apply the five lemma to the middle term.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that when the chaotic site is endowed with a sheaf of rings whose restriction maps are flat, the quasi-coherent modules form a weak Serre subcategory. The proof checks the defining property: it starts with a five-term exact sequence whose outer four terms are quasi-coherent, uses the base-change characterization of quasi-coherence on the chaotic topology, and considers the commutative diagram obtained by tensoring each term with O(U) over O(V); flatness of the restriction maps makes the two rows exact, so the base-change map for the middle term is an isomorphism by the five lemma, whence the middle term is quasi-coherent (proof lines 3606-3641). H2: the diagram chase through the five lemma, with flatness as the hypothesis that keeps the rows exact, is the substance.
